stories.title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 8 More Games In October
stories.summary: It's that time of month when Xbox updates the Game Pass library, and, as usual, a few more games are leaving the subscription service in a few weeks. On October 31, you can say goodbye to 8 more games, including a few LucasArts classics, a diggy-diggy blast of co-op fun, and one of the biggest Lego Star Wars games of all time. sources.title: XBOX Game Pass Will Remove 8 More Games in October
sources.text: The next set of games leaving the XBOX Game Pass library in October 2026 has been revealed, and players will see 8 more removed. When the first wave of XBOX Game Pass titles for October 2026 was announced, players learned that nine games would be removed from the library that month. As we approach the second wave of games, the next set of titles slated for removal has also been revealed. Check out the list below: As spotted by GameSpot , the list of games leaving XBOX Game Pass library has been updated, and the 8 games will be removed on October 31, 2026. One of the biggest titles that will be removed this month is LEGO Star Wars: Skywalker Saga, which is an action-adventure title that covers all the 9 Skywalker Saga movies in one game, with 300 playable characters to choose from plus 100 vehicles, 23 planets to explore, local and online co-op, and much more. Other than that, if you are a fan of Lara Croft, then Temple of Osiris could be a new experience to check out. It is the first-ever four-player co-op experience in the franchise, where players get to explore the Egyptian underworld. Players should note that they still have a few days to try the games out, and if they want to keep playing, they can also grab them at a discount. Here’s the full list of games leaving Game Pass in the second half of October: What are your thoughts on the eight games leaving Game Pass in October? Leave your thoughts down in the comments, and join the official Insider Gaming Discord server . For more information from Insider Gaming, read about The Finals adding dynamic commentary that says your actual player name . Don’t forget to sign up for our weekly newsletter .

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Xbox Game Pass Is Officially Losing One of the Best Star Wars Games of All Time This Month
sources.text: Two Double Fine games are also leaving as the studio goes independent. As October comes to a close and leaves fall from the trees, Xbox Game Pass is shedding more titles as a sign that this month is almost up. Xbox has revealed the second wave of titles leaving the subscription service on Oct. 31 (spooky), and while the list may be short, it has some absolute bangers you'll want to check out while you can. 2026 has been a great year for Star Wars games between Galactic Racer (what other game has Biddy Blas?) and Zero Company , though before these we had Lego Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga . The 2022 title includes all nine main films in charming Lego style, complete with the Lego games' signature co-op fun. The Skywalker Saga is one of the best Star Wars games, full stop. Grab a friend and marathon through it; you won't regret it. In addition to The Skywalker Saga , the newly independent (again) Double Fine has two point-and-click adventure games leaving the subscription service. These are Day of the Tentacle Remastered and Full Throttle Remastered . Tomb Raider fans should check out the isometric Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris , which is also slated to leave. The rest of the games set to be removed from Game Pass on Halloween are Dead Static Drive, Deep Rock Galactic, Wartales , and Wildgate . On Oct. 15, the first round of titles set to leave Xbox Game Pass this month were removed. The biggest loss was Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the turn-based RPG that was last year's GOTY darling. Here's the rest of the Oct. 15 list: Game Pass is in a state of flux right now as Xbox CEO Asha Sharma seeks to right the company's proverbial ship. Earlier this month, Windows Central obtained an internal memo in which Sharma reiterated that Microsoft's Game Pass strategy sent Xbox into "freefall." Ongoing changes aim to make the service better value for players while avoiding a drain on company resources. A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: Modern Warfare 4: Campaign Early Access Now Live

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Players on Steam so far seem delighted with Modern Warfare 4's campaign, making it one of the most well-received Call of Dutys in recent history
sources.text: It may be hard to believe, given all the Call of Duty: Modern 4 pre-launch community drama and the beta's lower-than-expected numbers on PC , but the final game may have turned things around - so far, at least. On Steam, Infinity Ward 's final chapter in the Modern Warfare sub-series currently has a Very Positive (92 percent) rating based on over 3,100 user reviews . Modern Warfare 4's campaign early access went live Friday, and the review rating has been improving steadily as players have experienced more of the campaign's missions. Many have likely finished it by now; the campaign is a little over six-hours in length, after all. Gaining access to the campaign on Friday required pre-ordering any of the game's editions digitally. Modern Warfare 4's official release isn't until 23rd October, which makes it hard to determine the current number of players, because SteamDB , our source for this data, can't reveal numbers without its tracking bot having a copy of the game. Setting aside player numbers, the sentiment around Modern Warfare 4 is considerably more positive at the outset compared to last year's Black Ops 7, currently sitting at Mostly Negative (37 percent) . While review ratings change over time with each major update, Modern Warfare 4 is currently the highest-rated Call of Duty in over a decade. However, it's worth bearing in mind that the people playing the game are likely the series' most keen players, so perhaps they're more lenient towards it. We haven't had a chance to review the game yet, having only received code late last week, but IGN published a COD: Modern Warfare 4 campaign review on Friday, scoring it 8/10. In the rebooted Modern Warfare series, the 2019 Modern Warfare game comes closest in average player sentiment with a Mostly Positive rating (79 percent) . 2022's Modern Warfare 2 is far lower with a Mixed rating (45 percent) . Outside of Infinity Ward's output, Black Ops: Cold War is close at Mostly Positive (79 percent) . Modern Warfare 4's next big moment is the anticipated release of DMZ, the game's extraction shooter mode. Like the campaign, DMZ is available early for pre-orders, unlocking tomorrow, 20th October . Finally, on 23rd October, traditional multiplayer becomes available, which is when we're likely to see a shift in user sentiment, if one is going to happen.

stories.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remaster rumoured, with leaker insisting it's not a remake
stories.summary: A remaster of cult 2004 RPG Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines may be in the works. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remaster rumoured, with leaker insisting it's not a remake
sources.text: A remaster of cult 2004 RPG Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines may be in the works. In a post on the r/GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit , a user wrote: "I can confirm that it is in the works. NOT a Remake, but a Remaster, with some caveats. That's all I can say". The poster says they have "previously leaked info on multiple other games", including that Forza Horizon 6 is set in Japan, but of course, all we can do is treat this as an unsubstantiated rumour for now. Their post follows an earlier thread about a possible Bloodlines remake, which they describe as having "kind of leaked" the news already. Separately, another post on the subreddit, flagged "Grain of Salt", links to a thread about the band Genitorturers, which was involved with the original soundtrack, mentioning a Bloodlines remake. ICYMI, Bloodlines 2 wrapped up development in June with its final post-launch update. The leaker also describes a "dire situation" in the games industry, saying they "expect many games that are in development right now to not see the light of day".

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Metal band Genitorturers claims a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is coming, getting a dozen crusty nerds way too worked up
sources.text: October 18: The original Reddit post has now been corroborated by Nicholas Golden of the industrial metal group GLDN , who were on the same October 15 bill at The Meadows with Genitorturers. Eurogamer also reports that a user on the Gaming Leaks and Rumors subreddit—who allegedly demonstrated insider knowledge of Forza Horizon 6 prior to release—also claims a VtMB remaster (not a remake) is in development. Original Story: This one is thin , man, but it has to do with one of my favorite games of all time , while the circumstances of the rumor are just kind of neat and weird, even if it turns out to be nothing. User Few_Interview8222 on the Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines subreddit reported back from a Genitorturers show in Brooklyn, New York. Partway through the set, the band supposedly told the crowd that a VtMB remake is happening. Genitorturers played at Brooklyn's The Meadows as part of their "Live + Lewd Tour" on October 15. We've reached out to both rights-holder Activision (one of several, it's complicated) and Genitorturers' representation, and will update this story if we hear back. In addition to a killer score by Rik Schaffer , Bloodlines featured wonderfully era-appropriate licensed tracks from metal bands⁠—they were mostly used as diegetic music in the nightclubs and bars of Los Angeles. The Genitorturers track Lecher Bitch was the pitch-perfect theme of The Last Round, a downtown LA dive bar frequented by the Anarch faction of vampires. Multiple commenters on the Reddit thread point out that this could have been a confused, untimely, misinterpreted, or all of the above reference to last year's Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2 . It's the sort of almost-but-not-quite thing you might expect from an artist with tangential awareness of a secondary fanbase they picked up over the years. A VtMB remake is also the sort of project you could see getting pingponged around between various actors and stakeholders: started, stopped, shopped around, etc. It'd be a situation ripe for collaborators on the periphery acting on outdated information. Rad! I think? It'd depend on who's doing it. More and more, I'm beginning to distrust anyone not named "Nightdive" when it comes to commercial remasters. See also: The recent Shogun 2 debacle and the fate of Deus Ex Remastered . Bloodlines is such a wild, janky, PC gaming package that Nightdive is the only studio I'd trust to not only do a remaster right, but also to bring on legendary modder Werner "Wesp5" Spahl, the man who's been keeping Bloodlines alive with one of the most impactful unofficial patch projects in gaming. A more ground-up remake would offer equally daunting challenges, like matching the one-of-a-kind mood and look Troika managed to evoke. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Bloodlines is one of my very favorite games and an incredible RPG that's well worth your time. To the uninitiated, I like to pitch it as an evolutionary missing link between 2D Fallout and New Vegas. Bloodlines boasts the open-ended design and reactivity of Fallout in 3D for the very first time (Bloodlines leads Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson were senior talent on Fallout 1). Unlike New Vegas' wide open world, however, Bloodlines had a more linear, but still loose sequence of zones on a world map to explore. Bloodlines' Y2K, gothic, noir interpretation of Los Angeles is one of the coolest worlds ever presented in an RPG. A Nightdive treatment would be my preferred outcome: build on Wesp5's work and compensate him accordingly, then make it more accessible on more platforms at a modest markup over the original game. Bloodlines 1 can be had for $20 on Steam and GOG , but it's practically always on sale. Even if it turns out to be nothing, this is still just a neat, newsworthy little incident to behold—Genitorturers shouting out an obscure, beloved RPG like this 22 years later, and maybe getting a couple genre nerds like me a little too excited on the way. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Ted has been thinking about PC games and bothering anyone who would listen with his thoughts on them ever since he booted up his sister's copy of Neverwinter Nights on the family computer. He is obsessed with all things CRPG and CRPG-adjacent, but has also covered esports, modding, and rare game collecting. When he's not playing or writing about games, you can find Ted lifting weights on his back porch. You can follow Ted on Bluesky . stories.title: Video Game Decomp Hub Closes Due To AI: ‘The Community Aspect Of Decompilation Has Been Broken’
stories.summary: An integral step towards mods, ports and patches, the popular decomp.dev decided the platform has been rendered obsolete by 'drive-by contributions'

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Video Game Decomp Hub Closes Due To AI: ‘The Community Aspect Of Decompilation Has Been Broken’
sources.text: When the major AI models updated in September, it seemed to usher in a tide of vibe coded havoc . The use of it in the modding community was divisive enough. Now dedicated platforms have been flushed and flustered by this new unprecedented wave. One popular platform, decomp.dev, has opted to throw in the towel . Not just because of how pervasive AI entries have become in their space, but for more philosophical reasons. They are a decompiling community, and they feel AI does not foster community. “It is now clear that, with the right guidance, human input, and code reviews, AI can expedite the decompilation process in a significant way,” writes the siteâs farewell message . “What is also now clear is that the community aspect of decompilation has been broken.” Founded in 2024, the site became a popular destination in the rapidly accelerating modding space. New tools and growing communities have made the rate of long-awaited translation patches and decompiles far more frequent, but the invasion of AI-generated decomps have fractured the scene. Decomp.devâs reasoning isnât anti-AI per se, but mournful in nature. Decompiling, in short, means disassembling and reassembling a game’s code. Once the structure is figured out, fans can construct all sorts of mods, ports and patches. The site’s closing statement says that recent models of Opus and GPT have been uncannily good at some of these practices, as if designed to do so. The consequence has been that anyone with a fistful of tokens can fish out their own. Decomp.dev feels that “drive-by contributions” have watered down the once collaborative spirit. If this is how things are going to be, then they feel a site such as this is obsolete. Itâs a new illustration in the continuing clash between those who enjoy these hobbies for camaraderie and those who want the most immediate, atomized experience imaginable. AI models may not have the ROM decomp communities in its sight but they certainly seem to be adept at cloning software. As reported by 404 Media in light of decomp.devâs closure, an AI suite from April was designed specifically to rip-off other programs within legally dubious frameworks. sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: One of the biggest game decompilation sites is closing because AI has ‘broken the community aspect’
sources.text: “Bad actors” are abusing open source decomps in “increasingly troublesome ways”, it says One of the biggest sites dedicated to video game decompilations is sunsetting due to the growth of AI. In recent years, fan developers have been taking on a number of ‘decompilation’ projects, in which they take an existing game and reverse-engineer it into readable code. These decompilations â which are technically legal because the developers do not use any leaked content or copyrighted assets, and require players to provide their own legally-sourced ROMs â open up the ability to improve games further with support for higher frame rates, widescreen and ultrawide aspect ratios, dual-stick controls and other user-made mods. The growth of AI has led to issues, however, with the community divided on whether using AI for these projects is a positive step (because it makes it much quicker) or a negative one. Now the website Decomp.dev , which indexes decompilations and tracks those projects currently in progress, will be ‘sunsetting’, as announced by its creator @encounter. In a statement posted on the site’s homepage, @encounter notes that while they don’t believe AI is the main issue in itself, because when used properly and ethically it “can expedite the decompilation process in a significant way”, the “community aspect of decompilation has been broken” by people using AI in more questionable ways. “Our projects have always been open source to encourage contributions and to benefit the community as a whole,” they wrote. “Bad actors have been abusing this in increasingly troublesome ways.” @example explained that some people have been taking existing decompilation projects which are currently in progress, forking them and “finishing” them with AI. “Every project works differently,” they wrote. “Some may not want to use AI for legal or ethical reasons, and others may be okay with AI, or use AI themselves, but do not want drive-by contributions from folks who have put no effort into making sure the contributions are good. “The bottom line is that these kinds of hostile forks put little to no effort into meaningfully contributing to existing projects, tearing apart our community fabric.” They also noted that anyone with a subscription to an AI service can now make a basic port or ‘static recompilation’ which functions at a basic level, but doesn’t make it possible to add any new features. “Compared to the decompilation process itself, porting is relatively easy, especially with the established tools written by talented humans,” they wrote. “While community members put in the effort to decompile a game, opportunists have frequently raced to release a half-baked, barely-functional port from it.” Finally, they stated that one of the main reasons for decompiling games was to learn and research how they were put together, and that too many people using AI to create instant PC ports are calling them decompilations when in reality they have no understanding of how the code works. “For years, decompilation communities attempted to establish that decompilation is primarily for research,” they wrote. “We love these games and want to understand how they work, and to uncover the mysteries that the original developers left behind. “That’s not to say that ports aren’t fun too, they’re just not the sole reason a decompilation exists. Sloptubers and subreddits like /r/decomps have done immense damage here, freely using ‘decomp’ to mean ‘PC port’.” @example noted that the site â which lists numerous in-progress decompilation projects and includes progress bars showing how far along they are â was originally designed as a motivational tool for developers, but has now turned into a high score table by people rushing out AI-assisted ports. “Decomp.dev was originally designed to gamify decompilation â watching the progress go up was a fun way to stay motivated when every fraction of a percent took real human effort,” they explained. “Today, that same idea has warped decompilation into a hollow numbers game, exacerbated by folks who just want to burn tokens to make number go up or ‘port game to PC’, all else be damned. “While the increased attention has brought in genuine folks who want to learn and contribute meaningfully, I believe that decomp.dev serving as a public index and leaderboard is now causing more harm than good.” The site will continue to track existing projects and will “serve individual project pages and historical data”, but the main index of decompilations and the ability to add new projects have now been disabled. @example stressed again that while AI “can help tremendously when used correctly”, too many people are using it for “slop”, which “comes in many forms, is hard to define and even harder to moderate”. “As a sole hobbyist, I don’t have the energy (or desire) to define what makes a ‘good’ decompilation and enforce that consistently across the hundreds of projects on the site,” they concluded.

stories.title: Samson studio Liquid Swords files for bankruptcy, staff reportedly unpaid for two months
stories.summary: Samson developer Liquid Swords has filed for bankruptcy after employees reportedly went unpaid for two months. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Samson studio Liquid Swords files for bankruptcy, staff reportedly unpaid for two months
sources.text: Swedish law firm Cirio acting as administrator, has filed a preliminary bidding document for developer Samson developer Liquid Swords has filed for bankruptcy after employees reportedly went unpaid for two months. The studio's administrator, Swedish law firm Cirio, published a preliminary bidding document for potential buyers last week. According to business site Breakit (via Game Talk ), employees petitioned for bankruptcy after not receiving pay for two months. Their salaries will be covered by the Swedish state wage guarantee . Earlier reports from Breakit stated that Liquid Swords faced "an acute liquidity shortage," with founder Christofer Sundberg commenting, "I don't think it can be resolved." All 27 employees are being dismissed as part of the bankruptcy. Cirio stated that their contracts "do not transfer with the business, and a takeover of staff requires that a buyer enter into new employment contracts with each employee." The preliminary bidding document stated that Liquid Swords' assets for sale "consist of intellectual property rights attributable to Samson," its debut title launched in April, "and the Company's other intellectual property, together with related development assets, equipment and inventory used in the Company's operations." The bidding window will conclude on October 21, 2026. Samson's unit sales and revenue were also included in the document. As of October 14, 2026, the game sold 151,900 copies, generating SEK 24.1 million ($2.4 million) in revenue. Avalanche co-founder Sundberg founded Liquid Swords in 2020 . In 2022, NetEase acquired an undisclosed minority stake in the company. Last February, Liquid Swords reduced its workforce for "the studio's long-term sustainability." The company did not specify how many employees were affected.

sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: Samson developer Liquid Swords is facing bankruptcy
sources.text: The studio behind open-world game has reportedly been declared bankrupt after months of unpaid developer wages Samson developer Liquid Swords has reportedly been declared bankrupt after its developers went unpaid for several months. According to Break It , the Swedish studio will now see the state step in to compensate its around 30 employees. At the same time, it hopes to find a buyer. Liquid Swords was co-founded in 2020 by Christofer Sundberg, who also co-founded Avalanche and was creative director on Just Cause. Its debut game, the open-world action title Samson, was released on Steam and the Epic Games Store in April to a mixed reception, with most criticism leveled at the number of bugs in the game. Sundberg later addressed criticism of the launch game , claiming that Liquid Swords âreleased a game with flaws for a number of reasons,â without explaining what those reasons were. âLaunching a game is a ton of work and Iâm proud of the effort our team has put into seeing Samson from its initial concept, through release,â he said, adding that Liquid Swords would âcontinue to keep our ears to the ground and improve the game with your supportâ. Samson was later released for consoles in September. In February 2025, the studio announced that it was making a round of layoffs , with Sundberg saying the company was in âa deeply regrettable position, with no choice but to begin the formal process of parting ways with some of our talented team membersâ

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Liquid Swords founder confirms that the Samson studio has closed
sources.text: "I've done everything I can to make this succeed." UPDATE 19TH OCTOBER: Liquid Swords founder and CCO Christofer Sundberg has confirmed the studio's closure. Writing on LinkedIn , Sundberg said the studio was in discussions with "all parties involved in Liquid Swords" about continuing support for Samson, and though there's nothing yet to announce, "it's something we're working to resolve". Sundberg also revealed that he's got plans to start a new studio "built with the current market in mind", and that he'll have more to share soon. "Liquid Swords is closing its doors. I've done everything I can to make this succeed, and I'm very proud of what we achieved together. "It's been a hell of a ride and a lot of fun, even when the circumstances gave us very little to laugh about. Building a studio, creating Samson and releasing it on PC and consoles took an enormous amount of work from people who cared deeply about what we were making. "The console versions met with much greater success than the PC release. We got them out, but that success wasn't enough to get the company across the finish line. Market conditions and some bad business decisions brought us here, and I own my part in that. I can look honestly at what went wrong and still be proud of what we built. "We're also in discussions with all parties involved in Liquid Swords about how we can continue to support Samson the way the game deserves. There's nothing to announce on that yet, but it's something we're working to resolve. "To everyone who worked at Liquid Swords, our partners and everyone who supported us and played Samson: thank you. You gave us plenty of reasons to keep fighting, and the work we did together deserves to be remembered for more than how the company ended. "We make mistakes, we learn, we fall, we rise up, we move on. That's sometimes a painful process, especially when it affects people you care about, but I refuse to give up. I never give up. "I'll be back at it again soon and will share more about my plans for a new studio. It will be built with the current market in mind, with a solid foundation and business decisions that give the games and the people making them room to succeed. The lessons from Liquid Swords will be part of how I build it.I still love making games. "There's a lot more I want to do, and I intend to get on with it." ORIGINAL STORY 18TH OCTOBER: Swedish studio Liquid Swords, maker of action game Samson, has reportedly been put into bankruptcy. Break It (thanks, PC Gamer ) reports that the studio's almost 30 employees will be compensated by the state, and that the bankruptcy trustee is looking for a buyer. The original report suggests Liquid Swords has not paid its developers for months, but the bankruptcy order, thought to have been issued on 12th October, should mean unpaid salaries will be covered by Sweden's state wage guarantee . Christofer Sundberg, who co-founded Just Cause developer Avalanche Studios , set up Liquid Swords in 2020. Samson: A Tyndalston Story, the studio's first game, launched on PC on 8th April, followed by PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on 21st September. The studio initially had difficulty securing a publisher, and reviews were ultimately mixed with players complaining of technical and performance issues. Liquid Swords is the latest studio hit by job losses. On 22nd September, Xbox confirmed 268 more layoffs and moved Rare and World's Edge under Activision, which will now develop the next Halo game, while Supermassive Games appears to have lost more than 70 staff earlier this month. Xbox also said that day it was beginning consultation on a proposed closure of Ninja Theory after two separate agreements for the studio fell through.

stories.title: Modder Uses AI to Put Shadow of War's Nemesis System in Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2
stories.summary: There’s a new Red Dead Redemption 2 mod inspired by Middle-earth: Shadow of War’s Nemesis System, which tracks how individual enemies feel about you.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Modder Uses AI to Put Shadow of War's Nemesis System in Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2
sources.text: A modder has used AI to put Middle-earth: Shadow of War’s Nemesis System inside Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 . The enRage mod, created by nicklovin99, tracks how individual enemies feel about you. This works largely the same way as Shadow of War's much-loved Nemesis System, creating rivalries on the fly and disrupting the ranks of rival gangs. And, like the Nemesis System, enRage names every single NPC in the game. Some like you, some fear you, and some want you dead. It groups people by gangs, groups, and affiliations, so you’ve got the O’Driscoll Boys, Lemoyne Raiders, the U.S. Army, The Klan, the Wapiti people, the Bronte Family, the Murfee Brood, the Skinner Brothers, Van der Linde, and unaffiliated randoms. These are all tracked in a new menu. When you kill an affiliated NPC, their status within the gang gets passed along to a new member in the organization. The Hierarchy menu page tracks every NPC in the game, and tells you how they feel about you. Then there’s the X-ray page, which allows you to see NPC skeletons and what injuries they carry, with limping and paralysis showing up as possible health conditions on the mod trailer. You can injure an enemy and hold them at gunpoint to use a new interaction menu, forcing them to tell you about another member of their gang. Like RimWorld, it also tracks interactions NPCs have with each other on another World page. It creates an illusion of the world moving on without you, with people adopting stray dogs, recovering from alcoholism, and starting new feuds with each other. Each NPC also has traits, such as calm, sharp, introverted, and, of course, drunk. It also tracks their faith — or lack of it, don’t tell Dutch — and what they do for a living. These clashing ideologies cause gang wars that wage with or without your involvement, and you can step in to help out either side or take care of two in one. Annoy a gang enough and they’ll send hunting parties after Arthur, making every trip across the open world perilous — it’s fertile ground for systemic stories. Early Access for the enRage mod is available now on Nexus Mods. nicklovin99 added a disclaimer to the mod's description, saying: "AI Transparency - Claude Code assisted in the creation of scripts and systems." The last few weeks have seen an explosion in AI-generated video game modding, with some using the technology to port games to a browser , mash two existing games together, or even make new games using existing, popular IP . Video game companies have reacted by issuing DMCA takedowns, but some have also issued statements somewhat in support of what's happening . And some even want a piece of the action. For example, last week, Xbox boss Asha Sharma announced Xbox Labs , a new initiative aimed at getting games on web browsers. It was seen as a reaction to the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved). "In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another," Sharma said. "These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models." Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.title: Red Dead Redemption e Bully quase não existiram, revela cofundador da Rockstar
sources.text: Dificuldades de desenvolvimento deixaram em risco dois grandes títulos do estúdio. Houser comenta que desenvolver jogos AAA já é um desafio por si só e, no caso de novas franquias, as dificuldades são ainda maiores. Por isso, a equipe responsável acaba se surpreendendo mais quando o título é finalmente lançado do que quando o projeto é cancelado. Ele revela que Red Dead Redemption enfrentou muitos momentos decisivos, mas conseguiu superar os obstáculos graças às “ pessoas fundamentais da equipe, que eram realmente fortes, mantiveram o foco no que estavam tentando fazer e resolveram os problemas ”. O principal deles, segundo Houser era “ desvendar o que havia de interessante em um jogo de mundo aberto sobre caubóis ”. Com o sucesso do título, que garantiu uma sequência maior e melhor em 2018, é um tanto “óbvio” perceber o que há de interessante no jogo, olhando em retrospecto. “ Mas, enquanto tudo acontecia, não havia nada além de espaços vazios que precisaram preencher aos poucos ”, acrescenta Houser.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation has a hard mode you can select from the start
sources.text: The Square Enix lead says "we’ve reimagined the high-difficulty experience to align with the new game design" Final Fantasy 7 Remake series producer Naoki Hamaguchi has confirmed details about Revelation's difficulty, including a new enemy strength option. Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth obviously have beloved combat in both entries, but neither game has combat I'd describe as particularly difficult. Obviously, tackling the Summon Materia battles from Chadley earlier than you're meant to is a bit of a nightmare, but for the core story progression, there were only a handful of moments when things felt much more challenging. And unfortunately, Hard mode was only made available after you beat the game in full, so unless you really want to replay it – which, given how long Rebirth is, I don't blame you for not wanting to – you won't experience it. Thankfully, Hamaguchi – in an interview with Hardcore Gamer – confirms that "Hard Mode is selectable from the very start of this game." He explained that the hard difficulty "won't function in the exact same way as it did in Remake and Rebirth" and that for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation "we’ve reimagined the high-difficulty experience to align with the new game design." "Unlike Remake and Rebirth, Revelation offers a wide variety of end-game content even after you’ve beaten the game," Hamaguchi explains, adding, "we aimed to create a game where players can enjoy various new content and challenges even after completing the main story." On top of that, the balance of hard mode has changed somewhat, with him explaining that player options "have expanded significantly," and, as a result, the team "determined that simply banning items wouldn’t be enough to achieve the ideal high-difficulty experience we envisioned." Hamaguchi also detailed an option in the difficulty settings, namely 'Enemy Strength,' which lets you choose between the returning Dynamic mode and static enemies. He explains, "we’ve created a challenging environment that will thoroughly satisfy those seeking high difficulty, while also expanding players’ freedom and strategic options." He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels. sources.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Lets You Play On The Hardest Difficulty From The Start Because Of The ‘Wide Variety Of End-Game Content’
sources.text: Difficulty Final Fantasy VII Revelation Settings The first two Final Fantasy VII remake games made Hard Mode a bonus reward you could only unlock by first beating the game. Final Fantasy VII Revelation dispenses with that approach and will make it an option from the start of the game. Thank the Ancients! “Hard Mode does indeed exist in Revelation , however, it wonât function in the exact same way as it did in Remake and Rebirth ,” Naoki Hamaguchi confirmed to Hardcore Gamer at TGS 2026 . “In Revelation, weâve reimagined the high-difficulty experience to align with the new game design.” Hard Mode is selectable from the very start of this game. Therefore, players who want to tackle challenging battles and high-difficulty gameplay right from the beginning can enjoy that experience from their very first playthrough. This is because, unlike Remake and Rebirth , Revelation offers a wide variety of end-game content even after youâve beaten the game. Rather than relying solely on the traditional flow of challenging Hard Mode after beating the game, we aimed to create a game where players can enjoy various new content and challenges even after completing the main story. In FINAL FANTASY VII REVELATION, weâve also included Dynamic Mode, just as in FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH, allowing players to enjoy consistently challenging battles throughout the game. – ãFFVII REVELATIONãã§ã¯ããFFVIIâ¦ https://t.co/hAc0ZHNz4E pic.twitter.com/bGEoLSnNV9 — æµå£ç´æ¨¹ /FINAL FANTASY VII REVELATION, April 8 2027 (@nhamaguc) October 19, 2026 One of the main things Hard Mode did to make the game harder in Remake and Rebirth was disable all item usage. Hamaguchi said that won’t be the case in Revelation due to more complex and strategic interactions with the combat and FITS job system . Square Enix has also kept Dynamic Mode from Rebirth , which keeps upping the challenge of enemies as players progress in the story no matter how powerful they get. Revelation ‘s developers had previously said that the final game in the trilogy would have a much easier Platinum Trophy to get on PlayStation 5, and allowing Hard Mode from the start answers my other biggest frustration with Final Fantasy VII Remake ‘s 100 percent completion achievements, namely that they required beating the game twice . I’ll be curious to see what kind of new bonus content Hamaguchi and the team has in mind to extend Revelation’s end game without forcing that second play through. Square Enix has also already promised story DLC for the game in the year after it launches . Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: GTA 6 será lançado em um mês! Vale a pena comprar na pré-venda?
sources.text: Após uma longa espera, vazamentos e inúmeros rumores, os fãs finalmente estão a poucos dias da grande estreia de GTA 6 . Isso mesmo, falta exatamente um mês para o lançamento do jogo mais aguardado de todos os tempos, que chega em 19 de novembro ao PS5 e Xbox Series X|S. Considerado um dos lançamentos mais aguardados da indústria, o título promete levar os jogadores de volta a uma nova versão de Vice City, desta vez acompanhando a história do casal Jason e Lucia. Com a estreia cada vez mais próxima, o VOXL preparou um guia para ajudar os jogadores a decidir se vale a pena comprar GTA 6 na pré-venda . O apanhadão a seguir reúne informações sobre o lançamento, as opções de compra e os principais pontos que devem ser considerados antes de garantir uma cópia antecipadamente. GTA 6 pode ser adquirido na PlayStation Store e na Microsoft Store em duas versões: Standard Edition por R$ 449,90 e Ultimate Edition por R$ 549,90 . Lembrando que o jogo também já pode ser encontrado com desconto nas varejistas — e os links estão logo abaixo. O game estará disponível no PS5 e Xbox Series S e X no dia 19 de novembro. Enquanto uma versão de PC deve chegar futuramente, o jogo não será lançado no PS4 e Xbox One. Além de garantir acesso ao game no lançamento, a compra antecipada de qualquer edição dá direito ao Pacote Vintage Vice City — que traz itens inspirados na era clássica de Vice City, incluindo veículo exclusivo, garagem personalizada e opções visuais para os protagonistas. O bônus inclui o sedã Vapid Stanier, roupas temáticas para Jason e Lucia e uma padronagem especial para armas inspirada no visual de Tommy Vercetti. Além disso, a pré-venda digital realizada pela PlayStation Store ou Microsoft Store garante um mês gratuito de GTA+. A assinatura inclui GTA$ mensais, descontos especiais, veículos exclusivos e acesso a uma seleção rotativa de jogos da Rockstar — e a lista completa de títulos você confere aqui . Rockstar divulga trailer de lançamento de GTA 6! Assista novo vídeo legendado em PT-BR A Ultimate Edition foi anunciada como a versão mais completa de GTA 6 e adiciona diversos conteúdos distribuídos ao longo da campanha . Segundo a Rockstar, os bônus estarão integrados à progressão da história de Jason e Lucia. Entre os destaques, estão veículos exclusivos como o Grotti Cheetah (1995), o Vapid Dominator Buggy e uma série de armas personalizadas. A edição também adiciona novas oficinas, atividades paralelas e missões especiais espalhadas pelo estado de Leonida. Os compradores ainda terão acesso a lojas exclusivas, tatuagens, roupas inéditas, penteados, embarcações, coleções de carros clássicos e conteúdos extras relacionados a facções presentes no universo do jogo. A Rockstar já confirmou que GTA 6 será vendido em mídia física no lançamento — mas com uma diferença importante em relação aos jogos tradicionais. Em vez de um disco, a caixa trará apenas um código para download do jogo . A empresa não explicou oficialmente a decisão, mas alguns fatores podem ter influenciado a escolha. Entre eles estão a prevenção de vazamentos antes da estreia, o tamanho do arquivo do jogo e a simplificação da logística de distribuição. Outro ponto é a redução dos custos de fabricação e transporte. Com um possível tamanho próximo dos 200 GB, a utilização de um código digital elimina a necessidade de múltiplos discos físicos dentro da embalagem. A pré-venda de GTA 6 pode ser interessante para quem pretende jogar desde o lançamento e aproveitar os bônus oferecidos pela Rockstar. Todas as edições incluem o Pacote Vintage Vice City, com veículo exclusivo, garagem personalizada e itens cosméticos para Jason e Lucia. Já a compra digital pela PS Store ou Microsoft Store também garante um mês grátis de GTA+, enquanto a Ultimate Edition adiciona veículos, armas, oficinas, atividades e missões especiais extras ao pacote. Por outro lado, quem não tem pressa para jogar pode preferir esperar. A pré-venda digital custa R$ 449,90 na edição Standard e R$ 549,90 na Ultimate, mas o jogo já aparece com descontos em algumas varejistas. Além disso, os preços podem variar após o lançamento, dependendo das promoções das lojas e de eventuais descontos futuros. Claro, não há garantias de que GTA 6 ficará mais barato logo na estreia, especialmente diante da expectativa em torno do jogo. Portanto, comprar antecipadamente faz mais sentido para quem quer garantir o acesso no primeiro dia e aproveitar os extras. Quem prioriza economizar pode acompanhar as ofertas e esperar por uma oportunidade mais vantajosa. Ansioso para GTA 6 ? Comente suas expectativas nas redes sociais do VOXL !
